subChunks.title: DISTINCT and Column Aliases
subChunks.hookHtml: Sometimes you want unique values only — no duplicates. Sometimes you want to rename a column in the result. DISTINCT and AS handle both.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
DISTINCT — remove duplicate rows

-- All ranks (with duplicates):
SELECT rank FROM apprentices;

-- Unique ranks only:
SELECT DISTINCT rank FROM apprentices;

DISTINCT applies to the entire row returned, not just the first column. SELECT DISTINCT rank, xp returns unique (rank, xp) pairs — which is rarely what you want.

AS — rename columns in the result

SELECT name AS wizard_name,
       xp   AS experience_points
FROM apprentices;

The alias exists only in the query result — it does not change the actual column name in the table. You can also alias expressions:

SELECT name, xp * 2 AS double_xp
FROM apprentices;

Table aliases

SELECT a.name, a.xp
FROM apprentices AS a
WHERE a.xp > 1000;

Table aliases become essential in JOIN queries to disambiguate same-named columns from different tables.

storyBeats.text: DISTINCT strips duplicate rows from the result. AS renames a column or expression in the output — the table itself is untouched. Table aliases become mandatory once you start joining ledgers; practise the habit now.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
🪄 Unique ranks

Return the list of distinct rank values present in the apprentices table — no duplicates. Order alphabetically.

guidedPracticeTests.label: Returns 4 distinct ranks
guidedPracticeTests.setup: CREATE TABLE apprentices (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, rank TEXT NOT NULL, xp INTEGER NOT NULL); INSERT INTO apprentices VALUES (1,'Alice','Apprentice',1200),(2,'Bjorn','Adept',2400),(3,'Cassia','Mage',4800),(4,'Dorian','Novice',80),(5,'Elara','Archmage',7500),(6,'Fenrir','Apprentice',950);

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain what DISTINCT does and why `SELECT DISTINCT rank, xp` might not return what a beginner expects.

options: Removes duplicate rows from the result set
Returns only the first row of each group
questions.answer: Removes duplicate rows from the result set
questions.explanation: DISTINCT eliminates duplicate rows from the output. It is placed immediately after SELECT and applies to the full combination of columns selected.

questions.prompt: Using the lesson data, how many rows does `SELECT DISTINCT rank FROM apprentices` return?
options: 4 (Novice, Apprentice, Adept, Mage — Archmage makes 5 but wait — let me check)
questions.explanation: The six apprentices have ranks: Apprentice (Alice), Adept (Bjorn), Mage (Cassia), Novice (Dorian), Archmage (Elara), Apprentice (Fenrir). DISTINCT collapses the two Apprentice rows, giving 5 unique ranks.

questions.prompt: What does `SELECT xp * 2 AS double_xp FROM apprentices WHERE id = 1` return for Alice (xp=1200)?
options: An error — expressions cannot be aliased
questions.explanation: SQL evaluates the expression xp * 2 and labels the result column double_xp per the AS alias.

questions.prompt: A developer writes `SELECT DISTINCT rank, xp FROM apprentices` hoping to see unique ranks. Why might the result be surprising?
options: DISTINCT applies to the full (rank, xp) pair, so rows are only removed if both rank AND xp are identical — it does not deduplicate by rank alone
DISTINCT on two columns returns no rows
DISTINCT cannot be used with more than one column
DISTINCT ignores the second column entirely
questions.answer: DISTINCT applies to the full (rank, xp) pair, so rows are only removed if both rank AND xp are identical — it does not deduplicate by rank alone
questions.explanation: To get unique ranks only, use SELECT DISTINCT rank. Adding xp means each unique (rank, xp) combination is retained — since all XP values differ, this returns all rows.
